rationale: The construction is internally at odds with itself — the archived burden ratio was motivated as a financing/distress risk premium, yet dividing by cash-flow volatility mechanically tilts the long leg toward the *safest* firms, and the X/VOL(·) design is essentially the same information-ratio template that already failed in the archive (ls_talpha 0.66), with an added blow-up risk when VOL approaches zero.

This is a pure window-length variant of the gen-0 winner with no new economic content, and the single-year denominator (oancf + xrd) frequently crosses zero, so the "coverage gain" mostly buys sign-unstable extreme observations that 1% winsorization will not tame.

target_name: Improving Cash Yield on Knowledge Capital
rationale: A genuinely distinct dynamic channel (direction of intangible productivity rather than its level or financing strain) that is coherently specified with cash flow to avoid the R&D-expensing mechanical link, though the 3-year stock plus 5-period trend requirement will likely push coverage below the already-thin 0.038 of the related level signal and small R&D denominators will dominate the tails.

The mirror-test logic is clean, but with R&D in the denominator the signal is largely a monotone inverse of R&D intensity, so a negative slope would be substantially explained by the long-known R&D-intensity return premium rather than by working-capital slack, making the intended discrimination between constraint-risk and quality interpretations unidentified.

R&D scaled by a capital-consumption proxy is close to a rediscovery of the established R&D-intensity/intangible-mismeasurement anomaly (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis, Lev-Sougiannis), with the depreciation deflator functioning as a cosmetic rescaling of R&D-to-capital rather than a new economic channel.

The expression contradicts the hypothesis: to make the accrual effect strongest where the knowledge stock is largest you must scale accruals *up* with R&D intensity, whereas dividing by TS_SUM(xrd,3) shrinks the signal for R&D-intensive firms and amplifies it (in both directions, muddling the sign) for firms with tiny R&D stocks.
